column1: # The production records that `run --tier resolve|full` cannot validate, classified
# exactly (roadmap A4, deferred-work item 14). Loaded by fixtures.load_classes(...,
# "production"): the same loader, key and stale rule as fixture-classes.tsv, whose
# header states them. A discrepancy, directive mismatch or representation violation can
# never be classified, and a classified record never counts as validated.
# case_id is `<corpus label>:<posix path relative to the corpus root>`. The labels are
# CORPORA in tools/config_oracle/__main__.py (bc-history, dc, bc28.1, bcapps-29.0). Only
# the entries for the requested roots are applied and stale-checked, so a run over one
# corpus leaves the others' entries alone; in the resolve tier, only entries whose reason
# is `resolver:` or `reference-error:` apply, the stages that tier runs.
# Every reason starts with its category (the loader enforces it; a bad one exits 2):
#   invalid-source:          the production source is not valid AL in that
#                            (a production file cannot compile without Base App symbols)
#                            whose `// Source <case_id>` line names this entry's input and
#                            whose `expect:` is a reject for every configuration covered.
#                            `evidence: alc manual, <when>` only where alc_probe cannot
#                            hold the input, and never with `*`.
#   debt(<owner>, <milestone>):  verification debt: <owner> is the roadmap sub-project
#                            that removes it, <milestone> the one it goes by (a
#                            sub-project id, or M3/M4/M5). The reason names the missing
#                            piece: the node type, and the host where there is one.
#   other:                   anything else. Every matched `other` entry is printed in the
# `# corpus-head <label> <sha>`: the corpus commit a label's entries were generated from.
# A requested corpus at another HEAD fails the run (exit 1, "regenerate it"): content-free
# would otherwise keep classifying a changed corpus. The oracle reads the working tree, not
# HEAD, so a modified, deleted or renamed tracked `.al` fails the run too (exit 1, files named).
# `# corpus-untracked <label> <sha256> <path>`: an untracked (or ignored) `.al` in that
# corpus's working tree, which the oracle reads. An untracked `.al` with no line, a sha256
# that differs, and a line whose file is gone (stale) each fail the run (exit 1). Other
# dirty files (parse outputs such as parsed.txt) are ignored. A label with no corpus-head
# line is not checked. Regenerate from a fresh full run (the A4 generator rewrites these lines).
